sources.authority: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government / Planning Data
sources.verified_fact: The production dataset listed 37,666 brownfield-land records from 354 providers; the collector last ran on 2026-07-20 and new data was last found on 2026-07-16.
sources.quality_effect: Adds a current official development-potential source while preserving the service warning that coverage may be incomplete and not yet cover all England.

sources.verified_fact: The Datahub combines planning applications and development proposals from all London Planning Authorities, updates records daily, and tracks permissions, starts and completions.
sources.quality_effect: Provides a live London development-pipeline source; records still require borough/GLA quality checks and exact spatial binding before parcel promotion.

sources.verified_fact: Opportunity Areas are London Plan growth locations, typically with capacity for at least 2,500 homes or 5,000 jobs, often linked to transport and infrastructure investment.
sources.quality_effect: Supports an area-level growth-potential component when an exact adopted boundary relation is documented.

sources.source: London Opportunity Area locations and boundary status
sources.verified_fact: The official map distinguishes adopted, emerging and boundary-to-be-defined Opportunity Area boundaries; locations without a defined boundary are approximate and subject to change.
sources.quality_effect: Prevents approximate or emerging OA locations from being treated as adopted parcel-level polygons.

sources.source: Planning Data public transport access nodes
sources.authority: Department for Transport data distributed through Planning Data
sources.verified_fact: The dataset listed 363,324 public transport access nodes and was refreshed on 2026-07-21, but the service states the current dataset was created by MHCLG and will be replaced when authoritative-source data is available.
sources.quality_effect: Useful for proximity preparation, but its origin limitation blocks use as sole high-confidence transport evidence.

sources.source: New local plan examination system guidance
sources.verified_fact: The Planning Inspectorate published guidance on 2026-06-18 for local plans under the new 2026 regulations, separate from the legacy examination route.
sources.quality_effect: Adds a plan-status gate so legacy and new-system plan evidence are not silently mixed.

sources.verified_fact: The GLA identifies Annual Monitoring Reports as the principal mechanism for assessing London Plan effectiveness and lists AMR 21, published January 2026, for the London Plan 2021.
sources.quality_effect: Provides aggregate trend validation, not parcel-level development evidence.
